A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same KAPPA research, with matching authors, title and retained experiments. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support comparison, including Appendices A–K in v1 and A–O in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original probing and intervention experiments on binary-choice benchmarks, free-form generation, general capabilities and subset-level analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds multi-option evaluations, model–probe agreement measurements and results on additional models.

M1.justification: v2 Section 3.3 extends the binary method with k-class knowledge and prediction probes and a matrix update that jointly aligns all option logits. This substantially expands the intervention procedure; the original binary update and its w/β variants remain.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluations identified as BBH-4C, MMLU-4C and ARC-3C in Table 3. These introduce decisions among more than two options within the retained benchmark families. Existing binary-choice, free-form BBH and vicuna-eval coverage remains.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains unchanged in the matched binary-choice, cross-dataset, free-form and general-capability experiments: Base, Steering, LoRA FT and BM25 ICL participate as before. The new multi-option and additional-model tables use the already evaluated Base and knowledge-probe comparators.

E3.justification: The new multi-option protocol uses eight sampled answer orders, one- and three-layer interventions, alignment scales of 30 and 20, and dataset-specific layer selections and learning rates (Appendix L). v2 also introduces model–probe agreement as an evaluation metric and adds model configurations spanning 4B–32B parameters. The original binary settings are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix G adds a direct diagnostic of whether the model's answer agrees with the knowledge probe after intervention. Existing hyperparameter sweeps, transformed-state visualizations, subset-specific probing and KAPPA-Scalar analyses remain; enlarged heatmaps do not constitute new analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seed-based replication, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty estimates. Answer-order and judge-order controls are retained; the additional multi-option permutations concern evaluation design rather than uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results in Tables 3, 8 and 16. Examples include BBH-4C accuracies of 27.6% for Base and 36.9% for three-layer KAPPA, and Qwen3-32B binary-BBH accuracies of 75.3% and 84.4% for Base and six-layer KAPPA. These are newly reported settings, not same-setting gains over v1. Retained binary tables, subset scores, Figure 4 results and general-capability win rates are unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix C adds a multi-output constrained optimization and Lagrange-multiplier derivation using an invertible Gram matrix under column independence. Appendix B also adds a rank-one factorization connecting KAPPA to LoRA. However, the augmented-state expression in Section 3.3/C.1 can modify the appended constant coordinate and is not generally equivalent to C.2's fixed-bias derivation.

C1.justification: General multi-option applicability changes from future work in v1 to an achieved central contribution in v2's abstract, introduction and conclusion. v2 also explicitly foregrounds causal mediation through a low-dimensional subspace and alignment between model answers and knowledge-probe outputs.

C2.justification: v2 reframes probe accuracy from an approximate upper bound on achievable performance to a measure of linearly extractable knowledge and an alignment target. It adds operational distinctions from LoRA and interprets smaller multi-option gains through smaller initial knowledge–prediction gaps. Existing qualifications about task-dependent subspaces and insufficient internal knowledge remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds dataset split counts, multi-option probe learning rates and intervention configurations, and general-capability sample counts and session details. It newly specifies intervention at every decoding step, names the free-form judge and states GPT-5's reasoning effort. These disclosures do not establish changes to retained experiments. The promise to release code upon publication is unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning around distractor-driven errors, inter-layer calibration and inference-time interventions, adding works such as Wiegreffe et al., Gottesman and Geva, Chen et al., and von Rütte et al. It adds explicit comparisons with fine-tuning and removes discussions citing Dathathri et al. and Lu and Rimsky. This exceeds the relocation of related work.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list and several results discussions are substantially rewritten. Related work moves before the method, experimental sections are reorganized around binary and multi-option settings, and explanatory material and appendix organization are expanded.

P2.justification: The compact probe heatmaps in v1 Figures 7–8 are enlarged and split into v2 Figures 7–10. Figure 4 is redrawn, including a free-form accuracy axis starting at 20 instead of zero, and probe legends are clarified. The general-capability table moves to Appendix N, while new result, agreement and configuration tables substantially expand the displays.

improvement.justification: The new agreement diagnostic and additional-model tests strengthen evidence for the original alignment mechanism, while added settings and enlarged heatmaps improve reproducibility and inspection. The multi-option extension addresses v1's restricted MCQ scope, but Section 3.3/Appendix C.1 can change the augmented coordinate defined as 1, unlike C.2's fixed-bias derivation. This inconsistency limits the net quality gain.
